requirements.text: Laws and Society. Discuss the following with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: Why we have criminal laws

children.label: (b)
children.text: The types of crimes, including property crimes, crimes against people, white collar crime, and environmental crime

children.label: (c)
children.text: Why people commit crimes

children.label: (d)
children.text: Why everyone should follow the law even when no one is watching

resources.title: Why Do We Obey Laws? The Social Contract (video)
Our Social Contract to Follow the Law (video)

children.label: (e)
children.text: The meaning of crime prevention

requirements.text: Groups Working to Prevent Crime. Research how the following groups contribute to crime prevention and share your findings with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: Citizens, including youth

resources.title: Neighbors: The Key to Crime Prevention (video)
How Sport Helps to Prevent Crime (video)

children.label: (b)
children.text: Schools

children.label: (c)
children.text: Neighborhood, social, and civic groups, including youth groups

resources.title: Youth Programs Teach Conflict Resolution Skills (video)

children.label: (d)
children.text: Private security

resources.title: Security Guards Reduce Crime in LA (video)

children.label: (e)
children.text: Law enforcement agencies

children.label: (f)
children.text: Courts

children.label: (g)
children.text: Corrections and rehabilitation programs

requirements.text: Crime in Your Community, State, and Nation. Do the following:

children.label: (a)
children.text: With your parent or guardian's permission and the approval of your counselor, research local, state, or national news coverage of three crimes of different types. Research how common these types of crimes are in your state or in the United States.

resources.title: What the Data Says About Crime in the U.S. and Substances (video)
Top 5 Common Crimes in the USA (video)

children.label: (b)
children.text: Record notes on which law enforcement agencies and courts were involved in the pursuit of justice for the victims and the accused person, why you think these crimes were committed, and what could be done to prevent similar crimes. Review your research with your counselor.

requirements.text: Home and Neighborhood Crime Prevention. Do the following:

children.label: (a)
children.text: Discuss the following with your counselor:
How participation in activities of families, churches, sports teams, and clubs prevents crime

resources.title: How Can Boxing Clubs Help Prevent Crime (video)

children.text: How designs of houses, neighborhoods, public buildings, stores, streets, and parks prevent crime

children.label: (b)
children.text: Conduct a security survey of a home, a neighborhood, a park, or a camp building with adult supervision and following youth protection guidelines using a security checklist in the Crime Prevention merit badge pamphlet or one approved by your counselor.

resources.title: 12 Ways to Protect Your Home While You're Away (video)

children.label: (c)
children.text: Use information from your survey for requirement 4(b) and the EDGE method to develop a lesson about how a family or Scouts can protect themselves from crime. Review your teaching plan with your counselor, then present your lesson to your family or to Scouts.

requirements.text: Retail Crime Prevention. Research the following topics and review them with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: The impact of shoplifting and employee theft (also known as shrinkage) and loss prevention on retail finances, customer service, and reputation

resources.title: The Impact of Shoplifting on the Retail Industry (video)

children.label: (b)
children.text: Techniques used by retail stores to prevent shoplifting

requirements.text: Reporting Crime. Discuss the following with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: When and how to report a crime or an impending crime

resources.title: How To Report a Crime—Public Safety Minute (video)

children.label: (b)
children.text: The warning signs for child abuse and domestic violence and how to report these situations

children.label: (c)
children.text: The three R's of personal safety and protection and how to apply them

children.label: (d)
children.text: How reporting a crime can help law enforcement provide resources for crime victims

requirements.text: Peers and Crime. Discuss the following with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: The role that peers play in crime, crime prevention, and experiencing crime

resources.title: Adolescent Risk-Takers: The Power of Peers (video)

children.label: (b)
children.text: How to resist peer influence

children.label: (c)
children.text: Bullying and hazing behaviors and signs that a friend may be bullying you or someone else

resources.title: Bullying and How To Stop It (video)

children.label: (d)
children.text: The impact of gangs on communities

requirements.text: Substance Use and Crime. Discuss the following with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: The legal and health consequences of using alcohol, tobacco and vaping products, illegal drugs, and diverted prescription drugs

resources.title: Drug Abuse, Causes, Signs and Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment (video)

children.label: (b)
children.text: How substance use contributes to violence and property crime and increases a person's risk of becoming a victim of crime

children.label: (c)
children.text: How drug abuse awareness, prevention, and recovery programs help prevent crime

children.label: (d)
children.text: How to get help if you or someone you know needs help with drugs or alcohol

resources.title: Finding Help for Drug and Alcohol Disorders (website)
Treatment Choices for Substance Use Disorders (video)

requirements.text: Online Crime and You. Discuss the following with your counselor:

children.label: (a)
children.text: How to avoid being the victim of online crimes

resources.title: Protect Your Personal Information From Hackers and Scammers (website)

children.label: (b)
children.text: Common online financial scams

children.label: (c)
children.text: Effective online security

children.label: (d)
children.text: Identity theft and how to prevent it

children.label: (e)
children.text: How criminals use social media to target victims

children.label: (f)
children.text: How bullying, texting, and sharing photos can become crimes

resources.title: Prevention: Learn How To Identify Bullying and Stand Up to It Safely (website)

requirements.text: Interview. With your parent or guardian's permission and your counselor's approval, interview a law enforcement officer or a civil servant about their work in crime prevention. Learn about how they chose this career and about their duties. Discuss what you learned with your counselor.

Careers. Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge in the field of crime prevention. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career.

resources.title: How Law Enforcement Agencies Serve the Public (video)
